set.approach: Aim for the north shore of Roosevelt Lake, beneath the North Ridge of Mt Conness. Parties get there from Tuolumne Meadows via Young Lakes and some cross-country travel, from Saddlebag Lake over the notch in the Conness North Ridge and down fourth-class slabs on its west side, or up the fourth-class chute used for the Conness West Ridge from Sawmill Campground. The route climbs the arete of the northernmost buttress. Ascend fifth-class slabs to a rocky gully left of the buttress and follow it to the base.
set.descent_text: Fourth-class ramps to the left or right of the summit block lead down to sandy slopes. From the plateau, the steep chute just left of the northernmost buttress goes to the north end of Roosevelt Lake, and an easy walk south reaches the south end of the lake.

set.approach: Park short of the seasonal gate and walk up the paved road to the point level with Gate Rock, then push through the brush to the boulder. The route is on the northeast side of the boulder, overhanging at the start and easing to slab at the top.

review.notes: Descent is stated on the Pepper Crack page as the boulder downclimb; applied to Gate Crack because it tops out on the same boulder. Reviewer may cut.

set.approach: Neanderthal Wall is the pyramid-shaped granite wall seen to the northeast on the drive north into Kernville. It needs a rugged hike, either from Chimney Peak Road on the north or from Fay Ranch on the south. The route starts a good way left of Cro-Magnon Man, up a crack that lies just right of a left-facing corner, then traverses right to a vertical crack system, water groove and chimney to the top.

set.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. The route is the third crack from the left on the north face, reached from the ledges below the corner.
set.descent_text: From the ridge at the top, scramble off to climber's left.

set.approach: Park at the Cliff Lake trailhead and follow the Cliff Lake trail to the lake. From there head east toward Bullfrog Lake and then to the base of Dogtooth Peak; depending on the time of year there may be river crossings. Traverse along the east face to the towers of exfoliating granite slabs on the southeast face, where a lightly used trail runs along the base, and watch for loose rock. The route starts directly left of the Lookout route, up a third and fourth class scramble from the big dead pine to the ledge with the first bolt.
set.descent_text: Scramble the last bit to the summit, then take the hiking trail down the northern side of the peak, which serves as the walk-off.

set.approach: The crag is on the reservoir shore and is easiest by boat or kayak from the launch, which has day parking; it can also be reached on foot from near the dam. The route is at the crag's north end, beside a class 4 gully, and starts from a good ledge up a thin to mid-width crack.
